chunks: In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful.
His command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says to it, 'Be,' and it is.
Glory be to You, O Allah, and with Your praise, I bear witness that there is no god but You, I seek Your forgiveness and repent to You.
ai.seo_question: What does the phrase 'Kun Fayakun' mean in Shia theology?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq utilizes this hadith to affirm the Shia doctrine of divine omnipotence, emphasizing that Allah’s command 'Kun' (Be) requires no intermediary or temporal delay, thereby refuting claims of necessity in creation. This concept is central to Shia kalām (theology) in distinguishing between God’s absolute will and the contingent nature of the created universe, reinforcing the immediacy of His decree.
